info.title: SQMeter REST API
info.summary: The REST API of an SQMeter sky-quality and safety monitor.
info.description:
Every `/api/*` route an SQMeter serves on port 80. Generated from the firmware's route registry and its contract schemas, so it matches the device.

**The same in every language**: numbers are JSON numbers with `.` as the decimal point, units and field names are never translated, and timestamps are Unix seconds or ISO 8601. Text for people (`reasons`, alert `title` and `message`, `error`) may be reworded between releases: key on `safe`, `reasonFlags` and the alert `event`.

**Password**: when protection is on, routes that change something need HTTP Basic auth with the device's username and password.

**ASCOM Alpaca** (`/api/v1/*`, `/management/*`) follows the ASCOM Alpaca standard and isn't repeated here: the device is a SafetyMonitor and an ObservingConditions device. See https://ascom-standards.org/api/.

get.description:
Firmware, memory, flash, time, WiFi (with IPv6 addresses), MQTT, Bluetooth, darkness, alerts, Alpaca clients, connections, sensor health and diagnostics. Also pushed over `/ws/status`.

Open: Read-only status for integrations.

get.description:
Every reading, with each group's `status` (`ok`, `stale`, `missing`, `error`). The same document as `/ws/sensors` and MQTT `<base>/state`. Groups for switched-off sensors are left out.

Open: Read-only readings for integrations.

Plain text `1` (safe) or `0` (unsafe): the SafetyMonitor verdict, for scripts and loggers.

Open: Read-only verdict for scripts.

The last 32 safety changes, device restarts and safe/unsafe alerts, newest first. Survives software restarts, crashes and updates, not power cuts.

Each setting that depends on another, and whether it's in effect or inactive, with the reason (spec 020).

The verdict served to Alpaca clients as `IsSafe`, with the reasons and the safe-delay countdown. Key on `safe` and `reasonFlags`; `reasons` is English text that may be reworded.

Open: Read-only verdict and reasons.

post.summary: Calibrate the light sensor's dark offset
post.description:
Stores the current rolling visible count as the dark offset. Cover the sensor first and wait for the averaging window to fill. 409 while it can't give a good offset (no readings yet, not in night mode, window not full).

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
Partial update: only the fields sent change. A masked or empty password keeps the stored one; `null` clears it. A wrong value is refused with `error` naming it; a setting whose dependency is off is saved and reported inactive by `/api/settings/effective`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
What the WiFi setup screen uses. Answers 202 at once; poll `/api/status` (`wifi.connectPending`, then `wifi.connected`). On success the network is saved and the device restarts onto it 15 s later. Send `""` as the password for an open network.

Needs the password when protection is on.

Queues a test on the given saved, switched-on channel(s); see `/api/alerts/recent` for the result. A channel that can't deliver right now is recorded as `skipped`. Add `event`, `level` and `sound` for a sample of that event, or `title`/`message` to try custom wording with `{variables}`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

ActionResult.title: Action result
ActionResult.description: What every action endpoint answers (spec 013 FR-009): on a 2xx status, success true plus details; on a 4xx/5xx status, an error message (an action may add its own details, e.g. the RG-15 test's raw response). Hand-written, not generated: tools/contract-check.py checks the device's actions against it.

clearInSeconds.description: Seconds until the rain hold releases; present only while rain has stopped but the clear delay holds it (spec 025).

Releases.title: Releases
Releases.description: GET /api/updates/check (src/WebServerUpdates.cpp, lib/ReleaseLogic): GitHub releases on the chosen track that have both a firmware file for this build and a web UI file for this partition layout, newest first. Hand-written, not generated.

WifiScan.title: WiFi scan
WifiScan.description: GET /api/wifi/scan (src/WebServerApi.cpp handleWiFiScan). The scan runs in the background: 202 with scanning true and no networks while it runs, then 200 with the list. Hand-written, not generated.
